info.title: Ruta 3D de la Alhambra en HTML

parts.text: Una ruta en 3D en la Alhambra de Granada en un solo fichero html Guarda lo que generes en la carpeta actual.

The user wants a 3D route in the Alhambra of Granada in a single HTML file. Let me check the current directory first. Let me think about what to build: A single HTML file with Three.js (probably via CDN import map) showing a 3D route through the Alhambra: starting at the Puerta de la Justicia / Plaza de los Alhambra, through the Patio de la Acequia, Court of the Myrtles, Court of the Lions, Hall of the Ambassadors, Mexuar, Partal, Generalife... with waypoints, camera animation following the route, narration. Let me check the directory and then write the file. I'll build with Three.js from CDN (unpkg/jsdelivr) using importmap for three.module.js and OrbitControls, plus maybe no extra libs. Let me first check the working directory. Plan: - Single HTML file: index.html in current folder. - 3D scene with: - Ground plane / terrain - Modeled buildings approximating Alhambra locations: Alcazaba (Torre de la Vela, Torre de la Justa), Nasrid Palaces (Comares Tower, Court of the Lions, Mexuar, Hall of the Abencerrajes, Court of the Myrtles/Arrayanes, Patio de la Acequia), Partal (Portico of the Drawbridge, Torre de las Damas), Generalife (Palace, Court of the Water Channel), Charles V's Palace (round courtyard), Church of Santa María, Alhambra gardens. - A route polyline through those waypoints with animated marker, camera flythrough. - UI: HUD with route list, play/pause, speed, narration text, minimap (2D canvas with top-down view of route), time-of-day slider, labels toggle. - Data about each stop: historical info. Given no internet assets, I must model geometry procedurally. I'll make a stylized "architectural model" look with procedural Islamic-style buildings: courtyard arcs, horseshoe arches, tiled walls, towers. Let me be careful about quality: the file will be long. Let's write a well-structured single file. Key features to make it impressive: 1. Procedural Alhambra layout — approximate relative positions (scaled). Use real-ish geography: - Coordinates (approx real, in meters, relative): - Plaza de los Alhambra (south entrance) at origin-ish (0,0) - Puerta de la Justicia (Torre de la Justa) north of plaza - Puerta de la Granja / Patio de los Arrayanes entry - Patio de los Arrayanes (Court of the Myrtles) with Comares Tower to the north - Court of the Lions to the east of Myrtles (Salón de Abencerrajes is west) - Hall of the Ambassadors inside Comares Tower (north of Myrtles) - Mexuar (courtyard of the Mexuar) north of Comares - Partal to the west: Torre de las Damas, Portico of the Drawbridge - Generalife to the northwest across the valley - Charles V palace (Palacio de Carlos V) west of the Nasrid palaces - Alcazaba to the west (Torre de la Vela) on the Sabika hill - Gardens of the Sultan / Jardines de la Alameda - I'll build a stylized top-down plan with these. 2. Route: 3D path with Catmull-Rom curve through waypoints, elevated slightly, with a glowing tube/line, animated traveling marker (like a "guide" light), and camera that follows in third-person. 3. Architecture: build with instanced/merged geometry for performance. Use simple box/cylinder meshes with materials: rammed earth walls (ochre), tile roofs (terracotta), tile panel decoration (colored squares via texture generated procedurally with canvas), slender columns with muqarnas-ish capitals, horseshoe arches (build via ExtrudeGeometry from shape or via torus segments + boxes). Simplified: build arches with a helper that creates a horseshoe arch from a lathe/shape extrusion. Use THREE.Shape with hole? Actually easier: create an arch "wall panel": a box wall with an arch-shaped hole (Shape with holes) extruded — gives real arched openings. That looks quite good. Let me plan the code structure: ```js // Palette const PAL = { earth:'#c9a26b', ... } ``` Texture generation via canvas: - tile pattern (azulejo) - grid of colored diamonds - stucco with subtle noise - roof tiles (red terracotta repeating semicircles) Building helpers: - `wallWithArches(w,h,depth, archW, archH, count)` → ExtrudeGeometry - `column(h)` → cylinder + capital box - `tower(r,h)` → cylinder with cone/roof - `courtyard(...)` - `garden(...)` with cypress trees, hedges, water channel Vegetation: low-poly cypress cones, hedges (boxes), flowers. Scene: fog, hemisphere + directional light with shadows, sky gradient (custom shader or just large sphere with gradient canvas texture). Also stars/moon if night. Minimap: 2D canvas drawing the plan: rectangles for building footprints + route polyline + marker. Good. Narration: array of stops with title, subtitle, text (Spanish), audio? No audio files; could use SpeechSynthesis API for narration (optional, nice touch) — but might be odd. I'll include an optional narration via Web Speech API toggle. That's a nice bonus and works offline in browsers. Time-of-day slider: changes sun position, sky color, light intensity, lamp glow at night. Let me also add: - Click on the route / waypoints to jump. - Progress bar of the tour with stop list, click a stop to travel there. - Keyboard: space play/pause, arrows speed. - "Modo vista" toggle: orbit free / first-person walk. First-person walk mode: camera at eye height 1.7m following route with WASD free look — that's more work. Simpler: "Vista del guía" (third person follow), "Cámara libre" (OrbitControls), "Recorrido automático" (cinematic path with look-at ahead). I'll implement three camera modes: 1. Libre (OrbitControls). 2. Guía (follow the traveler from behind). 3. Cinemática (camera flies along an offset path with slow look ahead). Implementation details for the traveler: a marker = a glowing sphere + point light + ring pulse. Route waypoints (2D plan coordinates, x east, z north; y up): Let me define in meters (scaled 1:1 roughly, maybe compress to fit). Real Alhambra spans ~400m x 200m. Fine. Let me write the file in pieces using write then edit? Better: write in one go, but that risks a huge single write. I'll write it in several chunks: create the file with write (HTML skeleton + CSS + start of script), then append sections using bash cat >> ... but instructions prefer write/edit tools. I can use write for the first chunk and edit to insert subsequent chunks (edit requires reading first — I wrote it so I know content; but tool says "You must use your Read tool at least once before editing" — that applies per file; I'll read after writing to satisfy). Let me design the code carefully. ### HTML structure ```html Alhambra de Granada — Ruta 3D
title, subtitle
stops list
controls: play/pause, speed, slider, time of day, view modes

...
``` Use unpkg or jsdelivr. Choose jsdelivr: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.160.0/build/three.module.js and addons at https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.160.0/examples/jsm/. Offline fallback: if module fails to load, show message. Also need OrbitControls from addons. Maybe safer to not depend on OrbitControls and implement my own simple orbit controls (~60 lines) to reduce dependency risk? But OrbitControls is standard and reliable. I'll implement my own minimal orbit controls to make the file work even if addons path fails... Actually with importmap, both come from the same CDN; if one fails both fail. I'll just use OrbitControls — it's fine. Hmm, but writing my own gives full control over damping & constraints and avoids version mismatch. I'll write my own lightweight controls (it's not much code) — this reduces external imports to just three core. Actually, let me use OrbitControls — well-tested, fewer bugs. But my own is like 50 lines and removes one failure mode... I'll use OrbitControls from addons (standard practice). Hmm — but the import of three in the addons file is `import {...} from 'three'` which works with importmap. Fine. ### Scene construction details Materials: ```js const MAT = { earth: new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({color:0xcbb089, roughness:0.95}), wall: ..., tilePanel: with canvas texture of azulejos, roof: terracotta with tile texture, stone: greyish, wood: dark brown, water: transparent blue with animated normal-ish (just opacity + slight specular), foliage: green, cypress: dark green, } ``` Textures via canvas: 1. `makeAzulejoTexture()` — 8x8 grid of tiles with different colors and simple geometric motifs (diamonds, stars). Used for dado walls, pools. 2. `makeStuccoTexture()` — noise speckle in ochre. 3. `makeRoofTileTexture()` — horizontal repeating rows of terracotta semicircles. 4. `makeGroundTexture()` — mottled earth/grass. Since textures repeat, set wrapS/T = RepeatWrapping and repeat per mesh. Need to clone textures with different repeats — use `tex.clone()` and set repeat. Geometry helpers: ```js function archWall(w,h,d, openings) // openings: array of {x, w, h} ``` Build a THREE.Shape rectangle w x h with holes being arch shapes. Hole shape: horseshoe arch outline. For a hole in a Shape, path direction should be opposite, but THREE handles holes regardless of winding? THREE.Shape holes: it uses ShapeUtils.triangulateShape; winding usually matters for the hole being subtracted — the library computes both holes and contour, should be fine as long as hole paths are defined; I'll construct hole path clockwise to be safe. Horseshoe arch: A horseshoe arch (arco de herradura) > semicircle, extending ~1/3 of radius below springing line. I'll approximate: shape of opening = rectangle of width w from y=0 to y=springing, plus arc: from angle 210° to -30° (i.e., arc extending beyond semicircle). Let me define: Given opening half-width a = w/2, arc radius R = a/ sin(θ/2)... Let's parametrize the horseshoe: the arch circle center at height yc = springing (top of vertical jamb). The arc spans from angle 200° to -20° (going through the top, i.e., from lower-left to lower-right over the top). At angle 200°, point = (R cos200, yc + R sin200) = (-0.94R, yc-0.34R). The jamb goes down from there vertically to y=0. For the arc to meet the jamb of width w at x=±a, we need R cos200 = -a → a = 0.94R → R = a/0.9397 ≈ 1.064a. Fine: R = a/cos(20°) ≈ 1.0642a. So opening outline: start at (-a, 0) → line to (-a, yc) → arc from angle 180°+? Hmm. Let's simplify: arch from angle 200° to -20°, center (0, yc), radius R. Points: P1 = (R cos200°, yc + R sin200°) = (-0.9397R, yc - 0.342R) = (-a, yc - 0.342R) since 0.9397R = a. Good, so the arc endpoint is exactly at x=-a, at height yc-0.342R (below center). Then vertical jamb down from (-a, yc-0.342R) to (-a, 0). Mirror on the right. So the hole path: ``` moveTo(-a, 0) lineTo(-a, yc - 0.342*R) absarc(0, yc, R, Math.PI + 0.349, -0.349, true)? ``` Hmm, arc from angle 200° to -20° going clockwise through 90° (top). In radians: start 200° = 3.4907 rad, end -20° = -0.349 rad. Going clockwise (decreasing angle) from 3.4907 to -0.349 passes 90° (top)? Decreasing from 200° → 90° → -20°: yes, that passes through the top. In three.js, `absarc(x, y, radius, startAngle, endAngle, clockwise)`. Passing clockwise=true from 3.4907 to -0.349 traverses decreasing angle. Good. Then lineTo(a, 0), close path. Wait: with clockwise=true and endAngle=-0.349 which is less than start, three's absarc handles it (it computes deltaAngle appropriately). Should be OK. Then the top of the hole: the apex is at yc + R. So total opening height h = yc + R. Given desired opening height h and width w: choose R = a/0.9397 (a=w/2), then yc = h - R. Must have yc > 0 and the horseshoe bottom-of-arc (yc-0.342R) > 0. With w=2.2, a=1.1, R=1.171, yc = h - 1.171. For h=3.5, yc=2.33 > 0.394. Good. Wall panel: create Shape rect(0..w, 0..h), add holes with offsets: holes are in shape coordinates, so translate x by -w/2 + opening center. Extrude with depth d, then rotate so it stands: extrude along +z then translate z=-d/2. Fine. Then `archWall` returns mesh with castShadow. Columns: cylinder r=0.13 h=2.6 + capital (box 0.3x0.18x0.3) + base. Courtyard quadripartite (Myrtles, Lions): 4 arcades around a square with corner pavilions. Let me build a generic function: ```js function buildArcade(width, height, bays, depth, opts) ``` Where bays = number of arches along the width. Each bay width = width/bays. Returns a group with the arched wall + columns at bay divisions. I'll use the archWall for the whole run (all openings at once) — efficient and simple. Let me define building blocks used for the Nasrid palaces: - `quadripartiteCourt(side, name)`: four arcades each of `side` length facing inward, plus corner chambers (boxes with roofs) — for Myrtles (side ~28m) and Lions (side ~26m). Lions has 28 columns in the court. Fine. - Fountain: 12 lions around a circular basin (use small boxes/spheres) + central dodecagonal basin. - Water channel (Acequia): long thin box of water with marble edges. - Comares Tower: big cube ~20x20x45 with smaller cube on top, tiled roof. - Mexuar: a rectangular court with a facade and a small domed room. - Sala de los Abencerrajes: hall with star-shaped vault (approximate with a dark ceiling) and a muqarnas-ish chandelier. - Partal: a tower (Torre de las Damas) with white plaster body and tiled dado, plus portico with arches. - Alcazaba: irregular walls, Torre de la Vela (cylinder with lantern), Torre de la Justa (square tower), Torre de la Pólvora. - Charles V palace: square ring building with circular inner court, two floors of columns (Renaissance), tiled roof. - Generalife: a palace block on terraces, Patio de la Acequia with long pool, gardens with cypresses, Patio de la Acequia channel. - Gardens: hedgerows, cypress cones, flower beds, fountains. Hmm the curve may cut through buildings; acceptable for a stylized model. I'll use Catmull-Rom curve through all waypoints (loop) with 'catmullrom' closed? I'd rather make it a closed loop so the tour ends where it starts. Let me make the path closed (loop=true) with all stops; the camera travels around it. Elevation: the path's y should follow terrain. I'll define terrain height function h(x,z): mostly flat around palaces, rising west/north to the Alcazaba hill and Generalife terraces, and dropping into the Darro valley (z ~ -105 region). Simple analytic function: ``` function terrainH(x,z){ let h = 0; // hill for Alcazaba (west) h += 8 * smoothstep(...) // valley along the Darro: a line from (-160,-100) to (40,-125)? ... } ``` Simpler: use a few Gaussian bumps/dips: - Alcazaba hill: center (-145, 35), sigma 45, amp 9. - Generalife terrace: center (-135,-145), sigma 40, amp 10. - Darro valley: a trough along a line; approximate with gaussian dip centered (-30,-110), sigma 35x18 rotated... Use gaussian: amp -8 centered (-40,-112) with sx=60, sz=16 → creates a valley crossing. - Generalife: also ridge between Alcazaba and Generalife. The ground mesh: a plane 600x600 with 200x200 segments displaced by terrainH. Vertex colors for grass/earth/stone depending on height & zone. The path y = terrainH + 0.35. Buildings sit at their zone's ground height (compute per building via terrainH at center). OK. Now the route needs to be drawn as a glowing ribbon: TubeGeometry along a slightly-offset CatmullRom curve (offset y+0.12) with emissive material, plus a wider translucent tube for the "glow" and a second thin bright core. Plus animated dashes? Could use a shader with time-based flow. Simpler: use a TubeGeometry with a texture of dashes scrolling (map with repeat + offset animation). Nice: create a canvas texture of a dashed stripe along u, repeat x = 60, animate offset.x -= dt*speed. Traveler: a group with a glowing sphere + light + animated ring; plus optionally a small stylized figure? A tiny marker is fine. Camera modes: - "Libre": OrbitControls enabled; camera free. - "Guía": camera behind traveler, looking slightly ahead, smoothing. - "Cinemática": camera offset from path using a parallel curve (e.g., path point + perpendicular offset of 18m, height 8m) looking at traveler ahead — gives a nice sweeping view. Let me write the code now. ```js import * as THREE from 'three'; import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js'; ``` Renderer setup with ACESFilmic tone mapping, sRGB output, shadowMap PCFSoft. Sky: large sphere with ShaderMaterial gradient (top color, bottom color, sun glow). Update uniforms with time of day. Sun: DirectionalLight; position computed from time of day (azimuth/elevation). At night, moonlight (dim blue) and lamp point lights (add a couple of PointLights in the palaces + emissive lantern spheres). Ground: PlaneGeometry with vertex displacement. Let me write the terrain function and then geometry builders. Important: keep code correct. Let me write the final file in parts. Part 1: HTML head, CSS, body markup, importmap, start of module (imports, constants, textures, utils). Part 2: builders (walls, arches, towers, courtyards, buildings). Part 3: site layout (plan data, route, labels, waypoints with narration). Part 4: camera, controls, animation loop, UI wiring, minimap. Let me write these carefully. CSS: modern dark UI with amber accents (Alhambra/Moorish vibe), Arabic-ish geometric accents via CSS gradients. Panels semi-transparent blur. Let me draft the narration texts (Spanish) — 12 stops, each ~2-3 sentences with historical info. Good content adds a lot of value. Texts: 1. Plaza de los Alhambra — "Puerta de las Granadas": Acceso a la ciudadela nazarí. La Puerta de las Granadas (1490) marca el inicio del recinto; más allá, la Puerta de la Justicia con su gcc. 2. Jardines de la Alameda: Jardín de la Reina (siglo XI), acequias,“李树” (palo de América/ junto al Generalife, llegados de América en el s. XVI) — In the Jardines de la Alameda there are "Árboles de la Reina" (Schinus molle) and a copy of the Puerta del Perdón from Córdoba. 3. Palacio de Carlos V:Built 1527-1637 by Pedro Machuca, Italian Renaissance, circular courtyard with 32 columns of two stories, clash with the Nasrid palaces. 4. Alcazaba: Fortress from the 11th c. (Al-Mu'tamid), Torre de la Vela (watchtower, bell 1840), Cuarto Dorado? Torre de la Vela offers the classic sunset view over the Darro and the Albaicín. 5.   const p0=new THREE.Vector2(Math.cos(rad(a0))*rOut, Math.sin(rad(a0))*rOut);

  s.closePath();
  const g=new THREE.ExtrudeGeometry(s,{depth:h,bevelEnabled:false,curveSegments:40});
  g.rotateX(-Math.PI/2);
  return g;
}

Now Part E: the scene setup (renderer, sky, lights), the route tube, the traveler, markers, labels, camera modes, animation loop, UI, minimap.

Key components:

```js
const canvas=document.getElementById('scene');
const renderer=new THREE.WebGLRenderer({canvas,antialias:true});
renderer.setPixelRatio(Math.min(devicePixelRatio,2));
renderer.setSize(innerWidth,innerHeight);
renderer.shadowMap.enabled=true;
renderer.shadowMap.type=THREE.PCFSoftShadowMap;
renderer.toneMapping=THREE.ACESFilmicToneMapping;
renderer.toneMappingExposure=1.05;
renderer.outputColorSpace=THREE.SRGBColorSpace; // default in r152+
const scene=new THREE.Scene();
scene.fog=new THREE.FogExp2(0xbfc9c8,0.0016);
const camera=new THREE.PerspectiveCamera(55,innerWidth/innerHeight,0.3,3000);
camera.position.set(60,80,160);
const controls=new OrbitControls(camera,canvas);
controls.enableDamping=true; controls.dampingFactor=0.06;
controls.maxPolarAngle=Math.PI*0.495;
controls.minDistance=4; controls.maxDistance=600;
controls.target.set(-40,6,-20);
```

Sky: sphere with a shader.

Sun: DirectionalLight + hemisphere light + ambient.

Stars: Points.

Route tube: 
```js
const tubeGeo=new THREE.TubeGeometry(curve, 700, 0.9, 10, true);
```
But the curve's y follows pathH ✓ (the curve is built from the nodes with pathH y). The tube will be at the path level ✓. However, at the bridge the path is elevated while the terrain dips → the tube floats above the valley, and the bridge structure is under it ✓ (bridge deck at y=0.6, path at 0.6 ✓).

Material: an emissive tube with a scrolling dash texture:
- Texture: a 64x8 canvas with a white dash.
- MeshStandardMaterial with map + emissiveMap + emissive color, transparent.

Let me do two tubes: an outer glow tube (radius 1.8, transparent additive, opacity 0.12) and the core tube (radius 0.55, emissive with a scrolling dash texture).

Traveler: a group with:
- a sphere (r=0.7) emissive gold
- a vertical beam (cylinder r=0.25 h=14, additive, opacity 0.25)
- a ring on the ground (torus, r=2.2, rotating)
- a PointLight (gold, intensity 2, distance 30)

Stop markers: for each stop, a cylinder pedestal + a numbered sprite + a small pillar of light. The number sprite: create a canvas texture per number.

Labels: HTML divs for the stops (name) and for the major buildings. Position them by projecting each frame.

Camera modes:
- 'libre': OrbitControls enabled; the traveler still moves.
- 'guia': camera behind the traveler.
- 'cine': an offset cinematic view.
- 'pea': first person.

Implement: in the animation loop, if mode != 'libre', set the camera position/target and disable the controls (controls.enabled = mode==='libre').

Transition: lerp the camera toward the target position for smoothness.

For 'guia': 
```js
const p=curve.getPointAt(u), t=curve.getTangentAt(u);
const desired = p.clone().add(new THREE.Vector3(0,0,0).sub(t.multiplyScalar(16))).setY(p.y+7);
```
Hmm: behind = p - t*14, elevated +5. Look at p + t*6 + (0,1.5,0).

For 'cine': a lateral offset: p + perpendicular*26 + up*14, looking at p + t*10.

Perpendicular: for the tangent (tx,ty,tz), the horizontal perpendicular is (-tz, 0, tx) normalized.

For 'pea': camera at p + (0,1.7,0), looking at p + t*10 + (0,1.7,0).

Smoothing: camera.position.lerp(desired, 1-Math.pow(0.001, dt)) — use a frame-rate-independent smoothing factor.

Also, when switching to 'libre', keep the current camera.

Tour progression: 
```js
let u=0, playing=true, speed=1;
const tourDuration=150; // segundos por vuelta a velocidad 1
u += dt*speed/tourDuration;
```
Since u is a normalized parameter (0..1) over the closed curve, and the curve's length is ~1300m, 150s → ~8.7 m/s (fast but cinematic). Let me use 170s.

Stop detection: precompute the u value for each stop node: find the closest point on the curve to the node position. I'll sample the curve at 1000 points and find the min distance to the node's position → u = index/1000.

Then track `lastU`; when u crosses a stop's u (with wraparound), show the stop's info.

UI:
- Build the stop list from STOPS.
- Play/pause, restart, speed cycling (0.5,1,2,4).
- View mode buttons.
- Time of day slider → update the sun/sky.
- Labels toggle.
- Voice toggle (speechSynthesis in Spanish).
- Minimap rendering each frame (or every other frame).

Minimap: canvas 240x252. Bounds: x from -195 to 105 (300), z from -185 to 155 (340). Scale = min(240/300, 252/340) = min(0.8, 0.741) = 0.741. Map: mx = (x-minX)*s + ox; my = (maxZ - z)*s + oy.

Draw:
- Background: transparent (the CSS gives it a dark bg).
- Terrain hint: draw the valley (a line), the river.
- Plan rects from PLAN.
- The route polyline.
- Stop dots (numbered) and the traveler triangle.

- 'Alcazaba' (-150, 40)

Plus the stop labels (numbered).

Projection: for each label, project its 3D position with the camera; if the z is within [-1,1] and the point is in front → show and position; else hide.

I'll write a helper to create label elements.

For the sun/time of day:
```js
function updateSun(h){
  const dayT = clamp((h-6)/14,0,1);   // 6:00 → 20:00
  const el = Math.sin(dayT*Math.PI)*0.95; // elevación
  const az = Math.PI*(0.15+dayT*0.85);   // ?
```
Let me define: the sun rises in the east (+x) at h=6 and sets in the west (-x) at h=20.
- az goes from 0 (east) to PI (west): az = PI*dayT.
- elevation angle = sin(dayT*PI) * 1.0 (radians, up to 90° at midday) — too steep; use max 65° = 1.13 rad: el = sin(dayT*PI)*1.13.
- The sun's direction vector: x = cos(az)*cos(el), y = sin(el), z = 0.45*sin(el)+0.25 (a southern arc).

At midday (dayT=0.5): az=PI/2 → x=0, el=1.13 → y=0.904, z=0.45*0.904+0.25=0.657. So the sun is high and to the south ✓.

At sunrise (dayT=0): az=0 → x=1, el=0 → y=0, z=0.25 → the sun is in the east, slightly south ✓.

Daylight factor: dayF = smooth(clamp(sin(el)*2.2,0,1))? Let me compute dayF = clamp(sin(el)*3,0,1) — full daylight when el is high.

Light intensity: sun.intensity = 0.2 + 3.2*dayF (the sun light color from warm orange at low elevation to white).
Sun color: mix(#ff9a4d, #fff6e0, clamp(el/0.8)).

Hemisphere light: sky color = mix(night blue, day blue) by dayF; intensity 0.35 + 0.8*dayF.

Sky shader uniforms: topColor/bottomColor from a palette by time:
- dawn (dayT<0.12): top #2b4f7a, bottom #f2a05e
- day: top #4b86c4, bottom #cfe3ee
- dusk: top #2a3f6b, bottom #ef8a4a
- night: top #070b16, bottom #101a2e
I'll interpolate based on the hour: use a simple function with a few keyframes.

Stars: visible when dayF < 0.25 (opacity).

import PIL.Image, numpy as np, sys

def ascii_art(path, cols=110, rows=42, label=''):
    im = PIL.Image.open(path).convert('RGB')
    w,h = im.size
    im = im.resize((cols,rows), PIL.LANCZOS)
    a = np.asarray(im).astype(float)
    lum = a.mean(axis=2)
    chars = ' .:-=+*#%@'
    print(f'--- {label} ({path}) lum min={lum.min():.0f} max={lum.max():.0f} mean={lum.mean():.0f} ---')
    for y in range(rows):
        line=''
        for x in range(cols):
            r,g,b = a[y,x]
            v = lum[y,x]/255
            c = chars[min(9,int(v*9.999))]
            # colorea un poco: verde/azul -> distintos caracteres
            if g > r*1.12 and g > b*1.05: c = 'o' if v<0.5 else 'O'
            elif b > r*1.18 and b > g*1.05: c = '~' if v<0.5 else '='
            line += c
        print(line)

if __name__=='__main__':
    for p in sys.argv[1:]:
        ascii_art(p)

parts.text:
Listo. He creado **`alhambra-3d.html`** (70 KB, un solo fichero) en la carpeta actual.

**Qué contiene**

- **Modelo 3D procedural** del conjunto (Three.js desde CDN vía `importmap`): Alcazaba con la Torre de la Vela, Puerta de la Justicia, Palacio de Carlos V con su patio circular de 32 columnas, Palacios Nazaríes (Patio de los Arrayanes, Torre de Comares, Mexuar, Sala de los Abencerrajes, Patio de los Leones, Mirador de Lindaraja), Partal, Generalife con la Acequia, puente sobre el Darro y la Alameda. Todo con arcos de herradura extruidos, mocárabes, azulejos y tejas generados por código.
- **Recorrido de 1,7 km** con 15 paradas narradas (texto histórico + consejo de visita), trazado luminoso animado y viajero que recorre la ruta.
- **Controles**: reproduce/pausa, velocidad (0,5×–4×), 4 cámaras (Guía, Cinemática, Peatón, Libre), deslizador de **hora del día** (cielo, sol, sombras y farolas cambian), etiquetas 3D, narración por voz y **minimapa** en vivo con el plano.
- Interfaz responsive en español, con carga animada.

**Verificación realizada** (Chrome headless): sin errores de consola, los 15 elementos de la lista y todos los controles responden, el salto entre paradas funciona y — mediante trazado de rayos sobre la geometría — confirmé que el itinerario **no atraviesa muros ni superficies**, salvo los arcos que atraviesa intencionadamente (puerta de la Justicia, pórtico de Carlos V, galerías).

Ábrelo con doble clic (necesita conexión a Internet para cargar Three.js desde el CDN).
